chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his men, who said:
The one who is obscene upon his Muslim brother, Allah would Remove the Blessings of his sustenance from him, and Allocate him to his own self, and Spoil his life upon him.

key_terms.بَرَكَةَ: Blessing, divine increase or benefit in something
key_terms.فَحُشَ: To be obscene, coarse, or display vulgarity in speech or behavior
key_terms.مَعِيشَتَهُ: His livelihood, means of living, or daily sustenance
key_terms.وَكَلَهُ: He left him, assigned him to be responsible for himself

ai.seo_question: What are the consequences of being obscene to a Muslim brother according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to highlight how linguistic misconduct directly impacts one's sustenance (rizq), linking spiritual purity with material well-being. The phrase 'left to his own self' (wakalahu ila nafsih) implies a state of divine neglect where the individual must bear the consequences of their coarse behavior without divine assistance, a concept deeply valued in Shia ethics regarding social conduct.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from one of his men who said,
‘The one who is obscene upon his Muslim brother, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Remove the Blessings of his sustenance from him, and Allocate him to his own self, and Spoil his life upon him’.
en.sarwar: 13. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from certain individuals of his people from who has said the following: “The Imam has said, ‘
Whoever uses foul language against his Muslim brother (in belief) Allah removes blessings from his livelihood, leaves him to be on his own and destroys his means of living.”’
